messages:
Nora: Quick RFC follow-up idea: what if we let the client supply a per-request "quality budget" and have the runtime pick the cheapest compatible precision profile? Seems useful for product teams that care about cost vs accuracy per-call.
Jakob: Interesting. So request header like: Quality-Budget: {mode: 'min_cost'|'guarantee_quality', pct: 0.5, metric: 'top1'}. Runtime chooses profile (fp8, int8, fp16) based on profile metadata.
Mei: We discussed similar in yesterday's meeting but didn't settle API shape. Key tradeoffs: atomicity (do we promise the chosen profile for whole request?), determinism (customer observability & reproducibility), and audit logs for compliance.
Carlos: Also need safety: if runtime picks low-precision and result fails downstream checks, how do we surface fallback? Do we re-run at higher precision synchronously (adds latency) or async recheck?
Nora: Proposal sketch in thread: client sends Quality-Budget header; runtime evaluates a small cost-quality table (per-model) and picks the profile; response includes Precision-Decision header with chosen_profile and an explanation token (estimate delta/ci). Example: "Precision-Decision: fp8-v2; expected_delta=0.6%".
Jakob: Ops: runtime must attach request tags so we can aggregate per-profile quality vs cost. Also expose a per-endpoint histogram of chosen_profile counts.
Mei: We need default policies for customers who don't send header (current behavior). Also an account-level policy to cap cheapest profiles for certain customers (e.g., enterprise opt-out).
Carlos: UX-wise, SDKs could provide a helper that maps business intent ("save_50pct_cost") to quality budget. But we must avoid encouraging heavy retries when quality fails.
infra-bot: Note: adding decision-time profile selection increases CPU on control plane (~0.4ms/request in our bench). Estimate ~2-4% cost overhead at peak.
audit-bot: Audit note: any per-request precision decision must be logged with a decision id and deterministic seed so we can repro decisions for compliance audits.
Mei: Security & privacy: the decision engine must avoid leaking customer workload characteristics in logs (mask prompt text). Keep decision metadata small and hashed if needed.
Nora: Fallback behavior options: (A) immediate synchronous fallback: re-run at higher-precision before returning (safer but costly); (B) optimistic return + background re-eval only for sampled requests (faster, but riskier); (C) staged: if confidence metric low, force sync fallback.
Jakob: I vote for C: runtime can compute a cheap confidence estimator (delta_ci) and only trigger sync fallback when estimator < threshold. That balances latency and quality.
Carlos: Add customer config: prefer_latency vs prefer_quality. prefer_latency means never sync fallback, prefer_quality means sync fallback on low-confidence.
Mei: Telemetry & metrics: per-request record: chosen_profile, confidence_score, cost_estimate, actual_quality_sample (if sampled). Dashboards need a profile-sliced SLO to show regressions over time.
Nora: Edge-case: chained calls and function-calling. If an LLM call triggers external side-effects, returning a low-quality result isn't acceptable. We should mark calls as "side-effect-safe" or not; if not safe, force higher baseline.
Jakob: Good point. Add a request flag side_effects_allowed:false default. SDKs/platform should set true only when safe. Runtime enforces: if false, lower bound profile = float64-like (or at least fp16).
Carlos: Implementation plan: 1) small API prototype (headers + response decision) + SDK helper (2 weeks), 2) runtime policy engine + decision log (3-4 weeks), 3) telemetry + dashboard (2 weeks), 4) opt-in customer beta.
Mei: Risks: decision nondeterminism across runtime versions; need versioned decision tables and stable hashing. Also a rollforward plan to disable budget-mode globally if regressions occur.
infra-bot: Action recorded: created ticket INF-3242 for decision engine perf impact and log schema.
audit-bot: Action recorded: created ticket AUD-198 for logging/audit requirements.
Nora: Next steps: Jakob will draft a concise RFC for header names, decision payload, and failure modes (ETA 3d). Mei will spec privacy/log masking (ETA 4d). Carlos will prototype SDK helper mapping intents->budgets (ETA 1w).
Jakob: I'll include sample header shapes and a fallback state machine in the RFC.
Nora: Thanks all. This could be a nice differentiator for cost-aware apps if we do the UX right.
